decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin m) is real m-dimensional Euclidean space with its usual Borel structure; Fin m indexes coordinates from zero. WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp preserve the entries. Ordinary finite function spaces and products carry product Borel structures and their usual default product norms.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) real is the full real orthogonal matrix group, with its usual topology and Borel structure, including either determinant sign. Matrix.PosDef means a real symmetric positive-definite matrix.

Measure.haarMeasure K is the canonical Haar measure normalized on the positive compact set K. TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts top is the entire compact group, so this constructor is its normalized Haar probability. Measure.restrict restricts a measure to a set; real nonnegative-infinite scalar multiplication has its usual meaning.

Matrix.reindex e e M has entries M (e.symm i) (e.symm j). Matrix.blockDiagonal f uses pairs (local coordinate, block index) and is zero between different blocks. Matrix.fromBlocks is the displayed two-by-two block assembly. finProdFinEquiv sends (a,b) to a times the cardinality of the second factor plus b; finSumFinEquiv concatenates its summands.

multivariateGaussian mean m covariance C is the pushforward of stdGaussian by z -> m + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (CFC.sqrt C) z. The covariance interpretation holds when C is positive semidefinite; otherwise this total constructor defaults to a point mass. Matrix inverse is totalized at singular matrices.

stdGaussian is the standard Gaussian obtained by independent scalar standard normal coordinates in an orthonormal basis. On a zero-dimensional Euclidean space it is the probability point mass at its sole vector.

Measure.map is measurable pushforward; Measure.bind integrates the displayed measure-valued family. Measure.pi and Measure.prod are actual finite independent and binary products. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one, and the almost-everywhere quantifier is with respect to its displayed measure. Natural division and remainder and real scalar arithmetic have their ordinary Lean meanings.

volume denotes canonical Euclidean Lebesgue measure; on ordinary finite function spaces and products it is the product of the component volumes. MeasurePreserving f mu nu means f is measurable and its pushforward sends mu exactly to nu.

Real Bochner integration is totalized (zero on nonintegrable input). Integrable denotes genuine L1 with respect to the displayed measure. Measurable is Borel measurability on these carriers. volume.withDensity (ofReal q) is the nonnegative density measure. ENNReal.ofReal truncates negative real inputs to zero; pointwise q nonnegativity is separately asserted. Real square root, exponential, norm and real powers have their usual Lean meanings.

Measure.real mu S means ENNReal.toReal (mu S), where finite values have their ordinary real values and infinity converts to zero. sSup of a set of real values is its least upper bound when the set is nonempty and bounded above; on an empty or unbounded set its total definition does not assert a probability-distance meaning. MeasurableSet denotes the given Borel event structure. These conventions alone do not assert finiteness, normalization, nonemptiness or boundedness.

    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let B : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
      fun O => ((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) -
        ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) +
          (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)
    let μ := (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let Dpos := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νpos)).map (fun Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Matrix.reindex e e
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => B (Os j))) 0 0
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)))
    let Dneg := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νneg)).map (fun Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Matrix.reindex e e
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => B (Os j))) 0 0
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)))
    let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    let Mpos := Dpos.bind γ
    let Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
    let δ : ℝ := sSup {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
      MeasurableSet B ∧ z = |Mpos.real B - Mneg.real B|}
    1 - Real.exp (-(((d / n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 8) *

For normalized full orthogonal Haar probability \(\mu_n\), let \(\nu_\pm=2\mu_n|_{\{\det O=\pm1\}}\). Define \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), \(\mathcal D_\pm=(\boldsymbol O\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r))_\#\nu_\pm^{\otimes k}\), and the actual averaged targets \(\bar\pi_\pm=\int\mathcal N(0,A^{-1})\,d\mathcal D_\pm(A)\). Total variation uses the source probability convention \(\delta=\sup_{B\text{ measurable}}|\bar\pi_+(B)-\bar\pi_-(B)|=\frac12\int|f-g|\,dx\). Nonempty/bounded event-supremum and mass-one density obligations are discharged by the canonical normalized-density theorem.

The proof uses actual ambient RN densities \(f=d\bar\pi_+/dx\), \(g=d\bar\pi_-/dx\), and actual block affinity \(a=\int\sqrt{p_+p_-}\). Absolute continuity, L1, normalization, the exact tensorization \(\int\sqrt{fg}=a^k\), and Eq25 are derived from existing canonical producers. They are not supplied as additional hypotheses.

The residual factor is included for \(r>0\); for \(r=0\), it is the zero-dimensional unit factor from the existing actual product-law and affinity producers. The theorem imposes no positive-remainder condition and includes all source-domain endpoints.

/-!
# Actual Gaussian-mixture TV amplification

Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2.3 Ex72 (final inequality).
The laws below are the actual determinant-component matrix-prior Gaussian
binds, and TV is the measurable-event supremum. Their probability and
absolute-continuity certificates identify event masses with genuine L1
RN-density integrals. The shared normalized-density comparison, actual Ex71
tensorization and actual Eq25 single-block estimate imply the stated bound.
No supplied density, integrability, probability or scalar-affinity premise
is added. The canonical producers include the zero-residual convention.
The oracle/query lower bounds remain separate.
-/
theorem actual_averaged_tv_lower_bound {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    letI : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
    let μ := orthogonalHaar n
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let Dpos := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νpos)).map (blockPrecision κ)
    let Dneg := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νneg)).map (blockPrecision κ)
    let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    let Mpos := Dpos.bind γ
    let Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
    let δ : ℝ := sSup {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
      MeasurableSet B ∧ z = |Mpos.real B - Mneg.real B|}
    1 - Real.exp (-(((d / n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 8) *
      Real.exp (-(10 * (n : ℝ)) / Real.sqrt κ)) ≤ δ := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
  let μ := orthogonalHaar n
  let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
    {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
  let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
    {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
  let Dpos := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νpos)).map (blockPrecision κ)
  let Dneg := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => νneg)).map (blockPrecision κ)
  let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
    fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
  let Mpos := Dpos.bind γ
  let Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
  let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
    fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
      Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
  let qpos : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νpos
  let qneg : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => ∫ O, p O x ∂νneg
  let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (qpos x * qneg x)
  let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    Real.sqrt (((Mpos.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal * ((Mneg.rnDeriv volume) x).toReal)

  let δ : ℝ := sSup {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    MeasurableSet B ∧ z = |Mpos.real B - Mneg.real B|}
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x => (Mpos.rnDeriv volume x).toReal
  let g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x => (Mneg.rnDeriv volume x).toReal
  -- Actual law probability is a canonical Ex6 output, not a new premise.
  have hp := AveragedBlockLaw.actual_averaged_block_product hn hnd hκ (b := 1) (Or.inl rfl)
  have hm := AveragedBlockLaw.actual_averaged_block_product hn hnd hκ (b := -1) (Or.inr rfl)
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure Mpos := hp.2.2.2.1
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure Mneg := hm.2.2.2.1
  have ht := AffinityTensorization.actual_affinity_tensorization hn hnd hκ
  have hb := SingleBlockAffinity.single_block_affinity_bound hn hκ
  dsimp only at ht hb
  -- RN integration over these actual finite laws has no infinity fallback.
  have hf0 (x) : 0 ≤ f x := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
  have hg0 (x) : 0 ≤ g x := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
  have hfm : Measurable f := (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv Mpos volume).ennreal_toReal
  have hgm : Measurable g := (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv Mneg volume).ennreal_toReal
  have hfi : Integrable f volume := Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv
  have hgi : Integrable g volume := Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv
  have hf1 : (∫ x, f x) = 1 := by
    calc
      _ = Mpos.real Set.univ := Measure.integral_toReal_rnDeriv ht.1
      _ = 1 := by simp [measureReal_def]
  have hg1 : (∫ x, g x) = 1 := by
    calc
      _ = Mneg.real Set.univ := Measure.integral_toReal_rnDeriv ht.2.1
      _ = 1 := by simp [measureReal_def]
  have hc := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.DensityAffinity.normalized_density_tv_affinity
    volume hf0 hg0 hfm hgm hfi hgi hf1 hg1
  dsimp only at hc
  -- Identify exactly the event supremum used in the source definition of TV.
  have hset : {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), MeasurableSet B ∧
      z = |(∫ x in B, f x) - (∫ x in B, g x)|} =
      {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), MeasurableSet B ∧
      z = |Mpos.real B - Mneg.real B|} := by
    ext z
    constructor <;> rintro ⟨B, hB, hz⟩
    · exact ⟨B, hB, (by rw [Measure.setIntegral_toReal_rnDeriv ht.1,
        Measure.setIntegral_toReal_rnDeriv ht.2.1] at hz; exact hz)⟩
    · exact ⟨B, hB, (by rw [Measure.setIntegral_toReal_rnDeriv ht.1,
        Measure.setIntegral_toReal_rnDeriv ht.2.1]; exact hz)⟩
  have htv : 1 - (∫ x, F x) ≤ δ := by
    have h := hc.2.2.2.2.1
    rw [hset] at h
    exact h
  -- Eq25 controls the true block affinity; Ex71 lifts it to the actual laws.
  have ha := hb.2.2.2.2.1.trans hb.2.2.2.2.2
  have hpow : a ^ (d / n) ≤ Real.exp
      (-(((d / n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 8) * Real.exp (-(10 * (n : ℝ)) / Real.sqrt κ)) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ (Real.exp (-(1 / 8 : ℝ) *
          Real.exp (-(10 * (n : ℝ)) / Real.sqrt κ))) ^ (d / n) :=
        pow_le_pow_left₀ hb.2.1 ha (d / n)
      _ = _ := by
        rw [← Real.exp_nat_mul]
        congr 1
        ring
  rw [ht.2.2.2] at htv
  exact (sub_le_sub_left hpow 1).trans htv
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.TVAmplification

reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers d and n with 3 ≤ n ≤ d, and every real κ ≥ 4, put q = ⌊d/n⌋ and r = d mod n. Work with real d by d matrices with their Borel measurable structure and with the usual Borel structure on real d-dimensional Euclidean space. Let O(n) be the full real orthogonal group, let μ be its Haar measure normalized to have mass one on the whole group, and define ν+ = 2 μ restricted to {O : det O = 1} and ν− = 2 μ restricted to {O : det O = −1}.

For O in O(n), define Bκ(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) I_n − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ). For each sign, take the q-fold finite product measure of ν+ or ν− on tuples (O_0, …, O_{q−1}), respectively. Send a tuple to the d by d matrix whose diagonal blocks are Bκ(O_0), …, Bκ(O_{q−1}), I_r, with zero off-diagonal blocks, using the coordinate order in which local coordinate a of block j occupies global coordinate jn + a, and remainder coordinate b occupies qn + b. Call these pushforward measures D+ and D−.

For each real d by d matrix A, let γ(A) be the multivariateGaussian constructor with mean zero and covariance argument A⁻¹. Let M+ = D+.bind γ and M− = D−.bind γ, where bind integrates this measure-valued family. Define Δ to be the real supremum of the numbers |toReal(M+(E)) − toReal(M−(E))| over all Borel subsets E of real d-dimensional Euclidean space. Then

1 − exp(−(q/8) exp(−10n/√κ)) ≤ Δ.

Here A⁻¹ uses totalized matrix inversion, including at singular matrices. The Gaussian constructor is the pushforward of the standard Gaussian by z ↦ CFC.sqrt(A⁻¹) z; the approved context gives it the covariance interpretation when its covariance argument is positive semidefinite and says that it defaults to a point mass otherwise. Thus merely supplying A⁻¹ as its argument does not itself assert that it is a covariance. The standard Gaussian in dimension zero is the point mass at the sole vector; an empty finite product and a zero-dimensional identity block have their usual finite-product and matrix meanings. For a measure value, toReal agrees with its finite real value and sends infinity to zero. The real supremum has its least-upper-bound interpretation when its defining set is nonempty and bounded above; the total supremum operation by itself does not establish these properties. In particular, this formulation does not silently replace Δ by a probability total-variation distance without establishing the needed finiteness and normalization. Natural-number division and remainder, real square root and exponential have their usual Lean meanings. The hypotheses give n > 0, q ≥ 1 and κ > 0, so no division by zero or square root of a negative parameter occurs in the displayed bound.

source.original_text: The total variation distance between the actual averaged Gaussian targets has the following explicit lower bound. \operatorname{TV}(\bar\pi_+,\bar\pi_-)\ge1-\exp\!\left[-\frac{\lfloor d/n\rfloor}{8}\exp\!\left(-\frac{10n}{\sqrt\kappa}\right)\right]. \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\ge4\); set \(k=\lfloor d/n\rfloor\) and \(r=d-kn=d\bmod n\). Both endpoint inequalities are inclusive. For normalized full orthogonal Haar probability \(\mu_n\), let \(\nu_\pm=2\mu_n|_{\{\det O=\pm1\}}\). Define \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), \(\mathcal D_\pm=(\boldsymbol O\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r))_\#\nu_\pm^{\otimes k}\), and the actual averaged targets \(\bar\pi_\pm=\int\mathcal N(0,A^{-1})\,d\mathcal D_\pm(A)\). Each product uses one common sign. Total variation uses the source probability convention \(\delta=\sup_{B\text{ measurable}}|\bar\pi_+(B)-\bar\pi_-(B)|=\frac12\int|f-g|\,dx\). In Lean, each event mass is \(M_\pm.\mathrm{real}(B)=\operatorname{toReal}(M_\pm(B))\); the actual laws are proved to be probabilities internally, so all event masses are finite. Nonempty/bounded event-supremum and mass-one density obligations are discharged by the canonical normalized-density theorem. The proof uses actual ambient RN densities \(f=d\bar\pi_+/dx\), \(g=d\bar\pi_-/dx\), and actual block affinity \(a=\int\sqrt{p_+p_-}\). Absolute continuity, L1, normalization, the exact tensorization \(\int\sqrt{fg}=a^k\), and Eq25 are derived from existing canonical producers. They are not supplied as additional hypotheses. The residual factor is included for \(r>0\); for \(r=0\), it is the zero-dimensional unit factor from the existing actual product-law and affinity producers. The theorem imposes no positive-remainder condition and includes all source-domain endpoints.
